name: Italian Game
description: Bishop to c4 aiming at f7, then the slow, flexible c3 and d3 plan.

lines.name: Giuoco Pianissimo (3…Bc5)

notes.4: Bc4 develops towards f7, the weakest point in Black's camp.
notes.6: c3 prepares d4 one day and takes d4 away from Black's knight.
notes.8: d3 protects e4 calmly; White keeps the centre solid and plays slowly.
notes.14: Bb3 keeps the bishop safe from …b5 and …Na5.

lines.summary: c3, d3, castle, Re1 and Bb3: a solid set-up, then slowly improve before breaking with d4.

lines.name: Knight tour Nbd2-f1

notes.4: Bc4 develops towards f7, the weakest point in Black's camp.
notes.6: c3 prepares d4 one day and takes d4 away from Black's knight.
notes.8: d3 protects e4 calmly; White keeps the centre solid and plays slowly.
notes.14: Bb3 keeps the bishop safe from …b5 and …Na5.
notes.18: Nbd2 starts the classic knight tour d2-f1-g3.
notes.20: Nf1 heads for g3, where the knight eyes f5 and supports the kingside.

lines.summary: The Italian knight tour: Nbd2, Nf1, Ng3, slowly building up before d4 or a kingside push.

lines.name: Early …d5

notes.4: Bc4 develops towards f7, the weakest point in Black's camp.
notes.6: c3 prepares d4 one day and takes d4 away from Black's knight.
notes.8: d3 protects e4 calmly; White keeps the centre solid and plays slowly.
notes.12: exd5 trades, so the black knight lands on d5 where it can be chased.
notes.14: Re1 puts pressure on the e5 pawn at once.

lines.summary: If Black plays …d5 early, trade on d5 and hit e5 with Re1.

lines.name: 4…Bc5

notes.4: Bc4 develops towards f7, the weakest point in Black's camp.
notes.6: d3 defends e4 and avoids the sharp theory after 4.Ng5.
notes.8: c3: the position is now the same as the Giuoco Pianissimo.

lines.summary: 4.d3 and 5.c3 bring the Two Knights back into the Giuoco: one plan for both.

lines.name: 4…Be7

notes.4: Bc4 develops towards f7, the weakest point in Black's camp.
notes.6: d3 defends e4 and avoids the sharp theory after 4.Ng5.
notes.10: Re1 adds support to e4 and gets the rook to the centre.
notes.12: c3 prepares d4 and gives the bishop a retreat on c2.

lines.summary: Against …Be7, the same plan: castle, Re1, c3, then think about d4.

lines.name: 7…Na5

notes.4: Bc4 develops towards f7, the weakest point in Black's camp.
notes.6: d3 defends e4 and avoids the sharp theory after 4.Ng5.
notes.10: Re1 adds support to e4 and gets the rook to the centre.
notes.12: c3 prepares d4 and gives the bishop a retreat on c2.
notes.14: Bb5 dodges the knight while keeping the bishop on the board.
notes.18: Bc2 tucks the bishop behind e4, eyeing the kingside.
notes.20: Nbd2 heads for f1 and g3, as in the Giuoco.

lines.summary: When …Na5 hits the bishop, keep it with Bb5-a4-c2, then do the Nbd2-f1 knight tour.

lines.name: Hungarian (3…Be7)

notes.4: Bc4 develops towards f7, the weakest point in Black's camp.
notes.6: d3 keeps things simple; after …Nf6 this is the Two Knights with …Be7.
notes.12: c3: the same position as Two Knights 4…Be7.

lines.summary: The Hungarian move order changes nothing: d3, O-O, Re1 and c3.

lines.name: Blackburne Shilling Trap (3…Nd4)

notes.4: Bc4 develops towards f7, the weakest point in Black's camp.
notes.5: …Nd4 is a trap: 4.Nxe5?? Qg5! wins material for Black.
notes.6: Nxd4 takes the knight instead of the e5 pawn; Black's centre pawn is pulled to d4.
notes.8: O-O and White is ahead in development, ready for c3 to attack d4.

lines.summary: Against 3…Nd4, don't grab e5: take the knight, castle, and use your lead in development.
